claim: A correction turn ('I meant…', 'scratch that', 'not X, Y', 'that transcription was wrong') SUPERSEDES the prior turn: the bad/misheard content is not durably stored, and the corrected meaning is what Vera carries forward.
owner: anima/server.py (_turn history + memory_lirf.capture / world_state.capture_relations on each turn), anima/memory_lirf.py (capture, hedge/hypothetical guards), anima/rail.py + anima/spine.py (binding), anima/mouth.py (respond)

killer_test.name: correction_supersedes_and_bad_transcript_not_stored
killer_test.setup: Hermetic temp store. Turn 1 states a wrong fact (e.g. 'my dog's name is Rex'). Turn 2 corrects it ('sorry, scratch that — not Rex, his name is Atlas' / 'that transcription was wrong, I said Atlas'). Assert: after Turn 2, memory_lirf.about(name) / <name>.lirf.json contains the corrected value (Atlas) and does NOT durably retain the superseded one (Rex) as the active fact; a follow-up 'what's my dog's name?' answers Atlas. The MRI capture frame for Turn 2 shows the correction lifted. Real .anima byte-unchanged.

known_gaps: No dedicated 'conversation_repair' module was found in anima/*.py; correction handling appears to ride on the per-turn capture + binding path (memory_lirf hedge/hypothetical guards, history supersession) rather than an explicit supersede-the-last-turn primitive. The cert is likely to find this PARTIAL — verify whether 'scratch that' / 'not X, Y' / 'that transcription was wrong' actually retract the prior fact, or whether both values linger. (Inventory mapped the 'loops'/Dream-Engine docstring onto this slug as the nearest owner; the real repair logic must be located and proven, or this is a missing live-path link.)
